Author: anfroholic
Content:
Looks like I'm putting some chips on the table regarding wirebonding exchange formats.

Currently have a few problems we need to solve. Right now everything is built around humans reading pictures. And in the age of AI, I think our formats should become more human-centric anyways.

### The premise
A picture is *already* the accepted exchange format today. So keep the picture as an SVG *(which is just XML under the hood)*, and embed wirebonding data directly as key/value pairs in the raw XML.
Proposed format is `myboard.wb.svg`
> Humans get what they want.
> Machines can read what they want.

What we've got so far:
- **Footprint export:** generates 3D models you can add to your board alongside your GDS (see attached). I'm also working on embedding the SVG data directly into the footprint itself.
- **GDS import:** finds the paths in your GDS and uses their names to help you create symbols and nets.
- **Multiple die and stacked die** support.
- **Any bond topology:** board to die, die to die, and everything in between.
- **import/export** of wb.svg files directly
- ...plus a bunch of other fun little tools.

Links and more info:
**App:** https://anfroholic.github.io/wirebonding.svg
**Repo:** https://github.com/anfroholic/wirebonding.svg

Feedback, ideas and issues are all welcome.

Example data:
```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:wb="urn:wbx:0.1" viewBox="-300 -500 19000 15600"
     wb:version="0.1" wb:units="um" wb:design="wafer.space 1x1 logo die" wb:rev="A"
     wb:rule-wire-gap="60" wb:rule-edge-clear="40">

  <!-- The board: an outline, and a land per bond finger. 1 unit = 1 µm, so this land is 250 × 1000 µm. -->
  <g>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="13000" height="13000" class="sub" wb:kind="outline" wb:name="SUB"/>
    <rect x="3175" y="10700" width="250" height="1000" class="cu"
          wb:kind="land" wb:name="L1" wb:net="clk_PAD" wb:finish="ENIG"/>
    <circle cx="900" cy="12100" r="250" class="cu" wb:kind="fiducial" wb:name="F1" wb:role="align" wb:datum="B"/>
  </g>

  <!-- The die, placed by its transform. Inside it, coordinates are the die's own, y up as in its GDS. -->
  <g transform="translate(4534 9061) scale(1 -1)" wb:kind="die" wb:name="U1" wb:gds-cell="chip_top" wb:pad-layer="37/0">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="3932" height="5122" class="die" wb:kind="outline"/>
    <g transform="scale(1 -1)"><title>U1 artwork</title>
      <image x="0" y="-5122" width="3932" height="5122" href="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo…"/>
    </g>
    <rect x="496" y="28" width="60" height="60" class="pad" wb:kind="pad" wb:name="1" wb:net="clk_PAD"/>
  </g>

  <!-- A wire from die pad U1.1 to land L1. stroke-width is the wire's diameter: 20 µm. -->
  <line x1="5060" y1="9003" x2="3300" y2="11000" stroke-width="20" class="w sig"
        wb:kind="wire" wb:name="W01" wb:from="U1.1" wb:to="L1" wb:profile="STD20"
        wb:seq="1" wb:tier="1" wb:net="clk_PAD"/>

  <!-- How the wire loops: a parametric profile that fits any span, drawn beside the plan. -->
  <g wb:kind="profile" wb:name="STD20" wb:material="Au" wb:style="ball-wedge" wb:dir="forward"
     wb:moves="180/0 30/12% -20/35%" wb:interp="spline" wb:ref-span="1000">…</g>

  <!-- Heights: the section view. Each rectangle's height is that layer's thickness: a 280 µm die. -->
  <rect x="4534" y="-305" width="3932" height="280" wb:kind="layer" wb:name="U1" wb:role="die" wb:material="Si"/>

  <!-- Where the die may land: a position tolerance to datums A, B and C. -->
  <g wb:kind="tolerance" wb:applies-to="U1" wb:char="position" wb:tol="50" wb:modifier="CZ" wb:datums="A B C">…</g>
</svg>
```

Author: h.tamas
Content:
- As Sylvain mentioned, SVG is tricky, especially when you want to read an SVG file written by a different program. You need to be careful with picking the right subset. AFAIU you only want one-way compatibility, i.e. you want general SVG software to _read_ .wb.svg, but you will only support reading files written by .wb.svg aware software. If so, I would make it more clear in the docs.
- Do you support non-axis-aligned rectangles as landing pads? They are useful for laying out pads along a circular arc to optimize max bond wire length vs. pad count, or to equalize the lengths of the wires.
- What's the suggested workflow? You draw the footprint in kicad, load it into the webapp, add the bond wires, export the .wb.svg and use it to regenerate the footprint? Is the .wb.svg the single source of truth? Shall I treat the kicad footprint as autogenerated? What happens if I need to manually edit the pad placement later on?
- Can I generate the footprint, 3d model, bondlist etc. from an unattended CI script instead of the webapp?
- I usually put some "extras" in my cob footprints: die attach pad, ground/power rings, silkscreen for glob top area, courtyard to keep other components away, fanout wires to connect the landing pads to the top-level grid etc. Where should they live? I wouldn't put them into an autogenerated footprint file because I don't want them to be overwritten. I don't want to bloat the .wb.svg spec with such features either. It would make sense to include the autogenerated footprint in my hand-drawn footprint, but kicad doesn't support nested footprints. Should I place two footprints on top of each other in the pcb layout? That might be the best solution, but I feel kind of meh.

Author: anfroholic
Content:
> [...] you want general SVG software to read .wb.svg, but you will only support reading files written by .wb.svg aware software. If so, I would make it more clear in the docs.
Noted, I will add that, thank you

> Do you support non-axis-aligned rectangles as landing pads? They are useful for laying out pads along a circular arc to optimize max bond wire length vs. pad count, or to equalize the lengths of the wires.
I have not tried that, but I'll add it to the list

> What's the suggested workflow? You draw the footprint in kicad, load it into the webapp, add the bond wires, export the .wb.svg and use it to regenerate the footprint?
Yes, regenerate the footprint and now it should contain all the data. The tool already exports a .kicad_mod footprint and/or .kicad_pcb board file. 
I am in the process of asking the kicad folks if `(type other)` is a stable enough place to hold this data. 
Fundamentally, my wish is that eventually no one ever needs to use the app and all this is just built into KiCad itself and any changes are automatically generated. But you've got to start somewhere, so here we are. 

> Can I generate the footprint, 3d model, bondlist etc. from an unattended CI script instead of the webapp?
Yes, that's my next task. I'll be uploading something to PyPI and you will be able to do all this from a script. Fundamentally, anyone consuming this would use the script to transform this into whatever format they desire. Earlier in the year I talked to a Yamaha rep and basically got "We don't tell out specifications to non-customers", but we know they're all different anyways, so this standard is designed to be as light as possible. 

> I usually put some "extras" in my cob footprints: die attach pad, ground/power rings, silkscreen for glob top area, courtyard to keep other components away, fanout wires to connect the landing pads to the top-level grid etc. Where should they live? I wouldn't put them into an autogenerated footprint file because I don't want them to be overwritten.
I think most everything is a `yes and` any of that data that's passed in is kept in the export, we're more just matching lands and pads with wires, adding some additional specs for the wires and feeding that back into the system. On the horizon is a symbol exporter as well. I think I would like to extract the pad labels and percolate them up to the kicad schematic level. 

> fanout wires to connect the landing pads
In the example picture I have here, you can land your chip onto a board. Fan out wires are more of a kicad_pcb thing  and not a footprint thing, this is a kicad specific limitation, but it should be handled as well. 

>  I don't want to bloat the .wb.svg spec with such features either. It would make sense to include the autogenerated footprint in my hand-drawn footprint, but kicad doesn't support nested footprints. Should I place two footprints on top of each other in the pcb layout? That might be the best solution, but I feel kind of meh.
I don't think I quite understand what you're trying to ask here? The two die ones are a bit tricky, not sure the best way to handle this currently...  Part of me wants to think that if you're generating a lot of this data from your GDS things are not likely to be changing a whole lot, but I could be mistaken. 

Takehome is: I want this to be incorporated into KiCad directly. If we play in the mud for a bit to work out the kinks, they'll be more likely to add it as a standard feature. Convincing board houses like NextPCB and others in the space to adopt wirebonding as a standard offering is another one of the main goals. 

Thanks for all the feedback, this is great!!

Author: h.tamas
Content:
I appreciate trying to bootstrap COB support with KiCad and NextPCB. I've designed the COB version of the Tiny Tapeout boards, so I've been following the KiCad feature requests and Stuart's behind-the-scenes work with getting the boards bonded, and certainly there's a lot of potential to improve on both fronts. And I agree that having an open format with some proof of concept software could help with adoption.

If the open source community is going to converge to this spec I assume that we will port our designs, so my comments come from having a look at our existing board files and checking for any gaps.

Here are a couple of our designs:
tt02: [pcb](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/breakout-tt02-cob) | [gds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-02/tt02/gds/user_project_wrapper.gds.gz)
tt08: [pcb](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/breakout-tt08-cob) | [oas](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-08/releases/download/tapeout-ci2409/caravel_2409485e.oas)
tt08 etr version: [pcb](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/breakout-ttsky-cob) | [oas](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-08/releases/download/tapeout-ci2409/caravel_2409485e.oas)
ttgf0p1: [pcb](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/breakout-ttgf0p1-cob) | [gds](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-gf-0p1/releases/download/v23/ttgf0p1_v23.fill.gds)
ttgf0p2: [pcb](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/breakout-ttgf0p2-cob) | [gds](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-gf-0p2/releases/download/tapeout-ws2512/tt_gf_wrapper.oas.tt_gf_wrapper.precheck.20251217_132152.output.gds)

Author: h.tamas
Content:
The circular-ish pad layout comes from some optimization pressure where we didn't know the exact design rules so we wanted to make everything as tight as possible to avoid any back-and-forth with the bonding house. I optimized TT02 "by hand" using SolveSpace, and the later iterations use an approximation of this optimum while being easier to generate [semi-automatically](https://github.com/TinyTapeout/cobbler). We also happen to like how it looks, but that's a secondary concern.

There are other points where I have issues with our current setup. It's not as automated as I'd like, and as you mention, the fanout wires would logically belong to the pcb level. I agree with that in principle, but when I actually tried, it became a nuisance to wire up the pads because the space is too tight for horizontal, vertical and 45° wires. Hence the workaround to include the fanout in the generated footprint and to designate them as irregularly shaped pads. (I have a design boundary where the pcb is manually edited and the footprint is mostly generated, so that changing some settings and regenerating the footprint wouldn't overwrite any of my manual work.)

Anyway, if all the bonding information is going to be embedded in the kicad footprint file and I can generate it in a scripted way and also export the diagrams, models and any other data for the foundry in a scripted way, then I think we should be fine (pending the non-axis-aligned landing pads).

And thanks for pushing for better COB support.
